output:
Sharing a recent experience with Sunbelt Charter Coaches so other planners can factor it into their CES-season transportation decisions.

For a client dinner on Thursday, November 5, we booked four coaches to transport 220 guests from their hotel to a ranch venue in Henderson, with pickup scheduled for 6:15 p.m. The booking was confirmed in writing twice, most recently on Tuesday, November 3. We paid the full $8,400: a 50% deposit in September and the balance seven days before the event.

Only two of the four coaches showed up. The first arrived 55 minutes late; that driver told me he had received the assignment at 5 p.m. The second coach broke down on the 215 with its AC out, leaving guests on the shoulder for approximately 40 minutes.

I ultimately put 60 guests into Ubers and Lyfts on my company card at a cost of approximately $1,900. Dinner began at 8:40 p.m. instead of 7 p.m., and the caterer charged overtime.

A late bus is something we can work around. Two missing coaches, a breakdown, and no backup plan or adequate communication are a different situation.

Sunbelt handled two smaller airport runs well for us last spring, which is why I trusted them with this booking. This experience was very different. Since Friday, my calls to the office have gone to voicemail, and I have not received a resolution to my refund request. I’m asking for a refund for the two coaches that never arrived, plus reimbursement for the rideshare costs.

My client is now reviewing whether to retain us for their March event. I can’t predict that outcome, but the transportation failures have put that relationship at risk.

Based on this experience, I would not book Sunbelt for a large event unless they can demonstrate that their dispatch, backup coverage, and communication issues have been addressed. I’m sharing the specifics because I know many planners here rely on them for airport and offsite transportation.
